name: TRAPPIST-1e
description: TRAPPIST-1e is an Earth-sized rocky exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of the ultra-cool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1. Liquid surface water and a protective atmosphere are highly probable.

name: Kepler-22b
description: The first planet discovered by NASA's Kepler mission to orbit in the habitable zone of a Sun-like star. Telemetry indicates a global, deep water ocean with no exposed solid landmasses.

name: 55 Cancri e
description: A carbon-rich 'super-Earth' orbiting extremely close to its star. The surface is covered in active silicate lava flows and molten carbon, creating a glowing red volcanic crust.

name: Kepler-16b
description: Known as a circumbinary planet, Kepler-16b orbits two stars instead of one. It is a freezing gas-and-ice world resembling Saturn, experiencing double sunsets and sunrises.

name: GJ 1214b
description: GJ 1214b is a super-Earth composed primarily of water, surrounded by a thick, steamy atmosphere of superheated water vapor under immense atmospheric pressure.

name: TOI-700d
description: An Earth-sized rocky exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of the red dwarf TOI-700. It receives 86% of the energy Earth receives from the Sun, making surface liquid water highly stable.

name: Kepler-452b
description: Often referred to as 'Earth's Cousin', Kepler-452b is a rocky planet orbiting a G2V star identical to our Sun. It is 1.5 billion years older than Earth, indicating a mature biosphere could exist.

name: OGLE-390L b
description: Orbiting a cool red dwarf at the far reaches of the galaxy, this super-Earth is locked in a permanent global ice age, with surface temperatures dropping close to absolute zero.
